slot.brief: shortest distance between two given skew lines; test coplanarity first, then apply the distance formula

stem: For the lines r = t(i + 2j + 2k) and r = i + s(2i + j - 2k), where t and s are real, the shortest distance between them is
working:
b1 x b2 = -6i + 6j - 3k; a2 - a1 = i; scalar triple product = -6; magnitude of cross product = sqrt(36 + 36 + 9) = 9; shortest distance = 6/9 = 2/3.

Independent check: Let a=(1,2,2), b=(2,1,-2), and p=(1,0,0). The distance is |p·(a×b)|/|a×b| = 6/9 = 2/3.
solution:
For two non-parallel lines, $d=\dfrac{|(\mathbf a_2-\mathbf a_1)\cdot(\mathbf b_1\times\mathbf b_2)|}{|\mathbf b_1\times\mathbf b_2|}$. Here $\mathbf b_1=(1,2,2)$, $\mathbf b_2=(2,1,-2)$ and $\mathbf a_2-\mathbf a_1=(1,0,0)$.
$$d=\frac{|(1,0,0)\cdot(-6,6,-3)|}{\sqrt{36+36+9}}=\frac{6}{9}=\frac23.$$
